```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Nguyen_2017_iv2cmt")()$meta$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12161>

Nguyen 2017 is the first tutorial of the ISoP Model Evaluation Group. Its
product is a catalogue of goodness-of-fit graphics and metrics (PRED / CPRED /
PPRED, WRES / CWRES / PWRES, IWRES, EBE plots, VPC, NPC, npd / npde) and a
proposed core set of evaluation graphs. That catalogue is not a model and is
not packaged.

To illustrate the graphics, the authors simulated data from two fully
specified "true" models and fitted the true model plus several deliberately
misspecified ones. The two data-generating models are packaged here:

* `Nguyen_2017_iv2cmt` -- the pharmacokinetic case example: a hypothetical drug
  given as a single IV bolus, two-compartment disposition, a binary
  concomitant-treatment effect on clearance and a weight effect on central
  volume (main text Eqs. 1-6; Supplementary Table S1).
* `Nguyen_2017_warfarin` -- the PK/PD case example: total warfarin after a
  single oral dose with a one-compartment, lagged first-order absorption model
  driving an inhibitory turnover model of prothrombin complex activity (PCA)
  (Eqs. 24-25; Supplementary Table S2).

The misspecified models (one-compartment, no covariates, no correlation,
constant or proportional error only; immediate-effect and effect-compartment
PD) were fitted to simulated data, and the paper prints no estimates for them,
so they are not packaged.

```{r models}
mod_pk <- readModelDb("Nguyen_2017_iv2cmt")()
mod_wf <- readModelDb("Nguyen_2017_warfarin")()
```

# Population

There is no real population. The PK case example simulates 180 virtual
subjects, 60 at each of 10, 100 and 1000 mg IV, sampled at 0.5, 1, 4, 12 and
24 h; body weight is Normal(70, 15) kg and half of the subjects receive the
concomitant treatment. The PK/PD case example simulates the design of the
O'Reilly warfarin studies: 32 subjects (27 male, 5 female) of 40-102 kg given
1.5 mg/kg orally, with total warfarin concentrations (mg/L) and PCA. The
subject weights and doses used below are those of the deposited simulated
dataset (`datafit.csv` in the Supplementary R codes and data).

```{r population}
str(mod_pk$meta$population)
str(mod_wf$meta$population)
```

# Source trace

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **iv2cmt** structure | 2-cmt, IV bolus, linear elimination | Eq. 1 |
| CL at CONMED_DRUGX = 0 | 0.1 L/h (Table S1 prints 1) | Supp Table S1; as-run value, see below |
| V1 at 70 kg | 0.5 L (Table S1 prints 5) | Supp Table S1; as-run value |
| Q | 0.1 L/h (Table S1 prints 1) | Supp Table S1; as-run value |
| V2 | 1 L (Table S1 prints 10) | Supp Table S1; as-run value |
| Concomitant-treatment effect on CL | `exp(0.5 * CONMED_DRUGX)` | Eq. 5; Supp Table S1 |
| Weight effect on V1 | `exp(0.75 * log(WT/70))` | Eqs. 5-6; Supp Table S1 |
| IIV | SD 0.5 on all four, corr(CL, V1) = 0.5 | Statistical model text; Supp Table S1 |
| Residual error | `(0.3 + 0.15 f)` SD | Eq. 3; Supp Table S1 |
| **warfarin** structure | 1-cmt, lagged first-order absorption, turnover PCA | Eq. 24 |
| CL, V at 70 kg | 0.135 L/h, 8.03 L | Supp Table S2 |
| Weight exponents on CL, V | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Eq. 25; Supp Table S2 |
| Absorption half-life, lag | 0.588 h, 0.842 h | Supp Table S2 |
| PCA0, C50, Teq | 96.6, 1.17 mg/L, 13.0 h | Supp Table S2 |
| Maximal inhibition | 1 (Table S2: -1, fixed) | Supp Table S2; sign discussed below |
| IIV variances | CL 0.0703, V 0.0195, Tabs 0.551, Tlag 0.347, PCA0 0.00286, C50 0.2, Teq 0.0114 | Supp Table S2 |
| Residual variances | PK additive 0.094 (mg/L)^2, proportional 0.00677; PCA additive 14.6 | Supp Table S2 |

# Part 1 -- hypothetical IV two-compartment drug

## Typical-value solve against the closed form

With all random effects at zero the model must reproduce the bi-exponential
solution of Eq. 1 for a bolus.

```{r pk-closed-form}
mod_pk_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk)
tgrid <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48)
ev_typ <- data.frame(
  id = rep(1:2, each = length(tgrid) + 1),
  time = rep(c(0, tgrid), 2),
  amt = rep(c(100, rep(0, length(tgrid))), 2),
  evid = rep(c(1L, rep(0L, length(tgrid))), 2),
  cmt = "central",
  WT = 70,
  CONMED_DRUGX = rep(0:1, each = length(tgrid) + 1)
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk_typ, ev_typ, addDosing = FALSE, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()

closed_2cmt <- function(t, dose, cl, v1, q, v2) {
  k10 <- cl / v1; k12 <- q / v1; k21 <- q / v2
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  alpha <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  dose / v1 * ((alpha - k21) / (alpha - beta) * exp(-alpha * t) +
    (k21 - beta) / (alpha - beta) * exp(-beta * t))
}
typ$closed <- with(typ, closed_2cmt(time, 100, ifelse(id == 1, 0.1, 0.1 * exp(0.5)), 0.5, 0.1, 1))
rel_err <- max(abs(typ$Cc / typ$closed - 1))
rel_err
stopifnot(rel_err < 1e-6)
```

## As-run values versus Supplementary Table S1

Supplementary Table S1 prints CL = 1 L/h, V1 = 5 L, Q = 1 L/h and V2 = 10 L.
The deposited simulation was not generated with those numbers. The geometric
means of the 180 deposited empirical-Bayes individual parameters, with the
covariate effects removed, are 0.102 L/h, 0.528 L, 0.113 L/h and 0.998 L. The
deposited figure script carries the true-model fit as 0.0977, 0.518, 0.113 and
1.01. Published Figure 1 shows observations up to about 4500 mg/L, which a
1000 mg bolus can reach only if V1 is near 0.5 L. The packaged model therefore
uses one tenth of each printed value.

Because all four disposition parameters scale by the same factor, the Table S1
values give the same curve shape at exactly one tenth of the concentration:

```{r pk-table-s1}
mod_s1 <- rxode2::ini(mod_pk_typ, lcl = log(1), lvc = log(5), lq = log(1), lvp = log(10))
typ_s1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_s1, ev_typ, addDosing = FALSE, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()
ratio <- typ$Cc / typ_s1$Cc
range(ratio)
stopifnot(max(abs(ratio / 10 - 1)) < 1e-6)
```

## Known-answer check against the deposited simulated data

The median concentrations of the deposited 180-subject dataset
(`pkdata_5pt_180.csv`, computed by the maintainers) are compared with the
median of a fresh cohort of the same design (200 subjects per dose).

```{r pk-cohort}
dep_pk <- data.frame(
  dose = rep(c(10, 100, 1000), 5),
  time = rep(c(0.5, 1, 4, 12, 24), each = 3),
  dep_median = c(13.93, 144.4, 1449, 12.55, 114.2, 1127, 3.896, 36.23, 360.6,
                 1.301, 13.96, 123.4, 0.6797, 7.456, 59.73)
)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170201)
n_arm <- 200
subj_pk <- data.frame(id = seq_len(3 * n_arm), dose = rep(c(10, 100, 1000), each = n_arm))
subj_pk$WT <- rnorm(nrow(subj_pk), 70, 15)
subj_pk$CONMED_DRUGX <- rep(0:1, length.out = nrow(subj_pk))
stopifnot(all(subj_pk$WT > 0))

ev_pk <- bind_rows(
  subj_pk |> mutate(time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  subj_pk[rep(seq_len(nrow(subj_pk)), each = 5), ] |>
    mutate(time = rep(c(0.5, 1, 4, 12, 24), nrow(subj_pk)), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dose, WT, CONMED_DRUGX)

sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, ev_pk, keep = "dose", addDosing = FALSE) |> as.data.frame()

cmp_pk <- sim_pk |>
  group_by(dose, time) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(sim), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(dep_pk, by = c("dose", "time")) |>
  mutate(log_ratio = log(sim_median / dep_median))
knitr::kable(cmp_pk, digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  # Structural: the Table S1 values would put every cell near log(10) = 2.3.
  median(abs(cmp_pk$log_ratio)) < 0.2,
  # Envelope over the 15 dose-time cells; robust to which subjects land in the tails.
  quantile(abs(cmp_pk$log_ratio), 0.9) < 0.4
)
```

```{r pk-figure, fig.cap = "Simulated individual predictions (grey) and their medians (line) by dose, with the deposited-data medians (points). Compare Supplementary Figure S1 of Nguyen 2017."}
# Individual predictions without residual error: the additive error makes some
# low concentrations negative, which a log axis cannot show.
ggplot(sim_pk, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = id), colour = "grey80", alpha = 0.4) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "line", colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data = dep_pk, aes(time, dep_median), colour = "red", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ dose, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)")
```

## PKNCA

The paper reports no NCA. Each simulated subject's AUC0-inf must equal
dose / CL_i for this linear model, which tests clearance, the covariate effect
on it and the bolus input together.

```{r pk-nca}
subj_nca <- subj_pk |> group_by(dose) |> slice_head(n = 60) |> ungroup()
nca_grid <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 168, 240, 336)
ev_nca <- bind_rows(
  subj_nca |> mutate(time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  subj_nca[rep(seq_len(nrow(subj_nca)), each = length(nca_grid)), ] |>
    mutate(time = rep(nca_grid, nrow(subj_nca)), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dose, WT, CONMED_DRUGX)
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, ev_nca, keep = "dose", addDosing = FALSE,
                           rtol = 1e-8, atol = 1e-10) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose, "mg"))

conc <- sim_nca |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
doses <- sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment, dose) |> mutate(time = 0)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_pk <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_pk)

auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_pk$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(sim_nca |> distinct(id, cl, dose), by = "id") |>
  mutate(ratio = PPORRES * cl / dose)
summary(auc_chk$ratio)
stopifnot(
  # Measured median 1.008: trapezoidal bias on the sampling grid.
  abs(median(auc_chk$ratio) - 1) < 0.03,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$ratio - 1), 0.9) < 0.1
)
```

# Part 2 -- warfarin PK and prothrombin complex activity

## The sign of the maximal effect

Eq. 24 prints the production term as `Rin * (1 - Emax * C / (C + C50))` while
Supplementary Table S2 gives `Emax = -1 (fixed)`. Taken together literally,
warfarin would *stimulate* PCA production. The deposited simulated dataset
shows the opposite: median PCA falls from about 96 at baseline to about 21 at
48-72 h (below). The packaged model therefore uses complete inhibition,
`kin * (1 - imax * Cc / (Cc + ic50))` with `imax = 1`, which is the magnitude
in Table S2 and the direction of the simulated data. The -1 is the sign
convention of the estimation software for an inhibitory effect.

## Drug-free steady state

```{r wf-baseline}
mod_wf_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_wf)
ev_base <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 24, 72, 144), amt = 0, evid = 0L,
                      cmt = "central", dvid = 1L, WT = 70)
base <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_wf_typ, ev_base, addDosing = FALSE) |> as.data.frame()
base$PCA
stopifnot(max(abs(base$PCA / 96.6 - 1)) < 1e-6)
```

## Virtual cohort

The 32 subjects of the deposited simulated dataset (the O'Reilly design),
replicated five times for 160 simulated subjects.

```{r wf-cohort}
subj_wf <- data.frame(
  WT = c(66.7, 66.7, 66.7, 80, 40, 75.3, 60, 90, 50, 70, 82, 75.3, 75.3, 50, 56.7, 58,
         78, 74.7, 63.7, 59, 62, 58, 73.3, 76.7, 74.7, 80, 80, 80, 102, 70, 83.3, 62),
  dose_mg = c(100, 100, 100, 120, 60, 113, 90, 135, 75, 105, 123, 113, 113, 75, 85, 87,
          117, 112, 95.5, 88.5, 93, 87, 110, 115, 112, 120, 120, 120, 153, 105, 125, 93)
)
c(range(subj_wf$WT), median(subj_wf$dose_mg / subj_wf$WT))

tobs_wf <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 6, 9, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144)
coh_wf <- subj_wf[rep(seq_len(nrow(subj_wf)), 5), ]
coh_wf$id <- seq_len(nrow(coh_wf))

make_wf_events <- function(coh, times) {
  bind_rows(
    coh |> mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_mg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    coh[rep(seq_len(nrow(coh)), each = length(times)), ] |>
      mutate(time = rep(times, nrow(coh)), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    # Two declared endpoints: every observation row nominates one with dvid;
    # both Cc and PCA are returned as columns at every observation time.
    mutate(dvid = ifelse(evid == 0L, 1L, NA_integer_)) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dvid, WT, dose_mg)
}

rxode2::rxSetSeed(1968)
sim_wf <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_wf, make_wf_events(coh_wf, tobs_wf), keep = "dose_mg",
                          addDosing = FALSE) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Known-answer check against the deposited simulated data

Medians of the deposited 32-subject simulated dataset (`datafit.csv`, computed
by the maintainers; times with at least 8 observations) against the medians of
the simulated cohort. `Cc` and `PCA` are the model predictions; the residual
errors are symmetric, so they do not move a median.

```{r wf-known-answer}
dep_cc <- data.frame(time = c(3, 6, 9, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120),
                     dep_median = c(8.194, 10.67, 11.05, 10.77, 9.255, 7.422, 6.267, 4.559, 3.274, 2.009))
dep_pca <- data.frame(time = c(0, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144),
                      dep_median = c(96.4, 36.71, 25.16, 20.52, 20.52, 25.42, 28.63, 43.0))

med_wf <- sim_wf |> group_by(time) |> summarise(Cc = median(Cc), PCA = median(PCA))
cmp_cc <- inner_join(med_wf |> select(time, sim_median = Cc), dep_cc, by = "time") |>
  mutate(log_ratio = log(sim_median / dep_median))
cmp_pca <- inner_join(med_wf |> select(time, sim_median = PCA), dep_pca, by = "time") |>
  mutate(log_ratio = log(sim_median / dep_median))
knitr::kable(cmp_cc, digits = 3, caption = "Warfarin concentration (mg/L)")
knitr::kable(cmp_pca, digits = 3, caption = "PCA")

stopifnot(
  median(abs(cmp_cc$log_ratio)) < 0.15,
  quantile(abs(cmp_cc$log_ratio), 0.9) < 0.4,
  # A stimulatory reading of Emax = -1 would put PCA above baseline, a log
  # ratio of about 1.5 at the nadir.
  median(abs(cmp_pca$log_ratio)) < 0.1,
  quantile(abs(cmp_pca$log_ratio), 0.9) < 0.25
)
```

## Typical profile (Figure 7b)

The population-prediction curves (red) of Figure 7b reach a PCA nadir of about
18-20 between 48 and 72 h and recover to about 40 by 144 h, for subjects of
about 70 kg given about 100 mg.

```{r wf-typical, fig.cap = "Typical-value warfarin concentration and PCA for a 66.7 kg subject given 100 mg. Compare the red PRED curves of Figure 7b."}
ev_typ_wf <- make_wf_events(data.frame(id = 1L, WT = 66.7, dose_mg = 100), seq(0, 144, by = 0.5))
typ_wf <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_wf_typ, ev_typ_wf, addDosing = FALSE) |> as.data.frame()
nadir <- typ_wf[which.min(typ_wf$PCA), c("time", "PCA")]
nadir
typ_wf$PCA[typ_wf$time == 144]
stopifnot(
  nadir$PCA > 12, nadir$PCA < 26,
  nadir$time >= 40, nadir$time <= 80
)

typ_wf |>
  select(time, `Warfarin (mg/L)` = Cc, `PCA` = PCA) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL)
```

## Visual predictive check (Figure 7d)

```{r wf-vpc, fig.cap = "10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of simulated PCA with residual error (lines) and the deposited-data medians (points). Compare Figure 7d."}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(1963)
ev_pca <- make_wf_events(coh_wf, c(0, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144)) |>
  mutate(dvid = ifelse(evid == 0L, 2L, NA_integer_))
sim_pca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_wf, ev_pca, addDosing = FALSE) |> as.data.frame()
vpc <- sim_pca |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(p10 = quantile(sim, 0.1), p50 = median(sim), p90 = quantile(sim, 0.9))
knitr::kable(vpc, digits = 1)
ggplot(vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = dep_pca, aes(time, dep_median), colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "PCA")
```

## PKNCA

The paper reports no NCA for warfarin. AUC0-inf must equal dose / CL_i, and
the typical terminal half-life is log(2) * 8.03 / 0.135 = 41.2 h.

```{r wf-nca}
nca_t <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, 192, 240, 336, 480)
coh_nca <- subj_wf |> mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
sim_wf_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_wf, make_wf_events(coh_nca, nca_t), keep = "dose_mg",
                              addDosing = FALSE, rtol = 1e-8, atol = 1e-10) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(treatment = "1.5 mg/kg oral")

conc_wf <- sim_wf_nca |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_wf <- sim_wf_nca |> distinct(id, treatment, dose_mg) |> mutate(time = 0)
nca_wf <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_wf, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_wf, dose_mg ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
summary(nca_wf)

res_wf <- as.data.frame(nca_wf$result) |>
  left_join(sim_wf_nca |> distinct(id, cl, vc, dose_mg), by = "id")
auc_wf <- res_wf |> filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |> mutate(ratio = PPORRES * cl / dose_mg)
hl_wf <- res_wf |> filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |> mutate(ratio = PPORRES / (log(2) * vc / cl))
summary(auc_wf$ratio)
summary(hl_wf$ratio)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_wf$ratio) - 1) < 0.02,
  quantile(abs(auc_wf$ratio - 1), 0.9) < 0.05,
  abs(median(hl_wf$ratio) - 1) < 0.05
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Hypothetical-drug typical values are one tenth of Supplementary Table S1.**
  The deposited simulation, the deposited figure script and published Figure 1
  all use CL = 0.1 L/h, V1 = 0.5 L, Q = 0.1 L/h and V2 = 1 L; Table S1 prints
  ten times each. The packaged model follows the as-run values; the Table S1
  values give the same curve at one tenth of the concentration (checked above).
  The deposited data do not reveal the exact as-run numbers, only their
  agreement to within sampling error with one tenth of Table S1.
* **The Table S1 IIV row label is missing.** The row reading 0.5 has lost its
  symbol in the published supplement; the Methods state that every diagonal
  element of Omega equals omega^2 with omega the SD, so each variance is 0.25.
* **Concomitant-treatment covariate.** The paper's binary "concomitant
  treatment" (Figure 1d: "co-administration with drug X") is carried as
  `CONMED_DRUGX`. The deposited files name this column `Sex`.
* **Residual-error forms.** The PK case example uses Eq. 3, SD =
  sigma_add + sigma_prop * f (`combined1`). For warfarin, Table S2 reports
  variances from a NONMEM simulation, and the variance-additive form
  (`combined2`) is assumed.
* **Warfarin maximal effect.** Encoded as complete inhibition (`imax = 1`); see
  "The sign of the maximal effect". Table S2 marks the Emax random effect as
  fixed to 0 and absent from the true model, so `imax` carries no IIV.
* **Absorption lag.** Eq. 24's piecewise absorption (no absorption before
  Tlag) is encoded with `alag(depot)`.
* **All values are `fixed()`.** They are the authors' data-generating
  constants, not estimates; the misspecified-model fits have no printed
  estimates and are not packaged.
* **PCA units.** The paper reports "PCA units"; PCA in the O'Reilly data is a
  percentage of normal activity.
* **Cohort weights.** Weight is drawn from Normal(70, 15) kg as stated, without
  truncation; the paper gives no bounds.
